site_description: A free, open source VPN client for Linux and macOS. Import your WireGuard .conf or OpenVPN .ovpn file and connect in one click. No account, no server.
footer_license: Tunnelbird is free software under the GPL-3.0, made by
home_title: Tunnelbird: WireGuard and OpenVPN client for Linux and macOS
hero_lead: Import the .conf or .ovpn file from your provider or your own server. Tunnelbird connects through your system's network settings: no account, no administrator password.
hero_soon_text: The first version is being finished. It will install in one command on Linux and macOS, with no store and no account.
hero_screenshot_alt: Tunnelbird connected to a tunnel in Amsterdam, with its public address, location and live traffic graph
demo_lead: Import the file from your provider, flip one switch, see where you appear to be.
demo_alt: Tunnelbird connected to a tunnel in Amsterdam, with its public address, location and live traffic graph
tab_linux_text: One command for every distribution. The script reads your system and picks the way that suits it: Tunnelbird's signed repository on Ubuntu, Debian, Mint and Fedora, so updates arrive with your system's, and a self-contained package on the others. No store, no account.
tab_linux_text_package: One command for every distribution. The script reads your system, checks what it needs and installs Tunnelbird in your home folder: no administrator, no store, no account. To update, run it again.
tab_source_text: You need Rust, GTK 4.14 and libadwaita 1.5 or later.
tab_windows_text: A native Windows app, built on the same core, is being written. It will be a free download from this site, with no store and no account.
tab_macos_text: The same command installs the native menu bar app on a Mac with Apple silicon (macOS 13 or later), in your Applications folder in your home folder. No store, no account. The first time you open it, it asks for your administrator's password once, to install its helper.
features_title: Everything you need, nothing to configure
wifi_title: Safe on café Wi-Fi, quiet at home
wifi_text: Pick the Wi-Fi networks you trust. Anywhere else, Tunnelbird connects your tunnel by itself. An optional check also recognises your own router, so a look-alike hotspot is not trusted.
wifi_alt: Preferences of the automatic connection: connect on untrusted networks, trusted Wi-Fi networks and the strict verification
f_traffic_text: Your public address, its country and city, and a graph of the traffic. Warns when the server goes quiet.
f_files_text: WireGuard® .conf and OpenVPN .ovpn files, checked and editable before anything is saved.
f_tray_text: Switch tunnels, watch the traffic and quit without opening the window.
f_phone_text: Share a WireGuard® tunnel as a QR code and scan it with your phone's VPN app.
private_text: No account, no tracking. The only requests are the location of your public address while connected, and a daily check for new versions you can turn off.
linux_text: Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, Mint, Arch and more, on Intel/AMD and ARM, with GNOME, KDE and others.
install_page_lead: Pick your system. One command installs Tunnelbird on Linux and on macOS; Windows comes later.
install_soon_lead: Tunnelbird is not available yet. Here is how it will install on each system.
steps_title: Step by step, without the script
steps_lead: What install.sh does, one command at a time, to type yourself.
steps_package: Self-contained package, step by step (what the script does)
requirements_text: Linux with NetworkManager (installed by default on desktop distributions). For OpenVPN profiles, NetworkManager's OpenVPN plugin: Tunnelbird shows the command to install it if it is missing.
uninstall_text: Remove the app the way you installed it. Your tunnels stay in your system's network settings until you delete them.
download_text: Packages for amd64 and arm64 come with each release on GitHub, with their checksums. Prefer the repository above: a downloaded package gets no updates.
download_text_package: The release holds a package for amd64 and arm64 and its checksums (SHA256SUMS), plus .deb and .rpm files for people who build their own repositories.
docs_lead: Everything Tunnelbird does, in plain words.
docs_start_1: Get the file of your tunnel: your VPN provider's website, your router, or your own server (wg-easy, PiVPN…) gives a .conf (WireGuard®) or .ovpn (OpenVPN) file.
docs_start_2: In Tunnelbird, click + or drop the file on the window. A preview shows what was read: check it, give the tunnel a name, and import.
docs_start_3: Turn the switch on. Your system may ask for your password once, to allow network changes.
docs_openvpn_text: Profiles with their certificates inside work as they are. If the profile refers to separate files (ca.crt, client.key…), select them together with the .ovpn file. When the server asks for a user name and password, type the user name in the preview; leave the password empty to be asked at the first connection, and your desktop keyring keeps it.
docs_trust_text: In Preferences › Automatic Connection, choose a tunnel and the Wi-Fi networks you trust, picked from the ones your computer already knows. On any other network, Tunnelbird connects the tunnel by itself; it never disconnects anything on its own. The strict verification also checks the router's hardware address, so a hotspot named like your home network is not trusted.
docs_share_text: The share button of a tunnel saves it as a file, or shows a WireGuard® tunnel as a QR code for your phone's VPN app. Both contain the tunnel's private key: keep them to yourself.
docs_tray_text: Tunnelbird keeps running in the top bar when its window is closed (Preferences › Run in Background). On GNOME, the icon needs the AppIndicator extension, enabled by default on Ubuntu; KDE shows it natively.
docs_updates_text: On Ubuntu, Debian, Mint and Fedora, updates arrive with your system's; elsewhere, run the install command again. Tunnelbird tells you when a new version is installed and offers to restart, then shows what's new.
docs_updates_text_package: To update, run the install command again. Tunnelbird tells you when a new version is installed and offers to restart, then shows what's new.
docs_trouble_server: “The server does not answer”: the tunnel is up but nothing comes back. Check the server address and that your network allows its port.
docs_trouble_plugin: “OpenVPN support is not installed”: install the command Tunnelbird shows, then connect again.
docs_trouble_more: Something else? Open an issue on GitHub with what you did and what you saw.
privacy_lead: Tunnelbird asks for nothing and keeps nothing about you.
privacy_app_1: No account, no analytics, no tracking, no advertising.
privacy_app_2: While a tunnel carrying all your traffic is connected, Tunnelbird asks ifconfig.co, through the tunnel, for your public address and its approximate location, to show where you appear to be. This reveals nothing more than any website sees.
privacy_app_3: Once a day, installs made with the script or from a downloaded package ask this site for the latest version number. Nothing about you is sent, and Preferences can turn it off.
privacy_app_4: Your tunnels and keys stay in your system's network settings, readable by the system only.
privacy_site_text: No cookies, no analytics, no third-party content: fonts and images come from this site. Your theme and language choices are kept in your browser only.
changes_lead: Every version of Tunnelbird, newest first.
compat_lead: What Tunnelbird runs on, and what was really tested.
compat_legend: “Tested” means run on a real machine. “Expected” means every requirement is met but it was not tried yet.
compat_cpu_arm: ARM 64-bit (aarch64): Raspberry Pi 4 and 5, ARM laptops
compat_desktop_text: The window works with any desktop, on Wayland and X11. The top bar icon needs a StatusNotifierItem host: built into KDE, Cinnamon and others; on GNOME, the AppIndicator extension (enabled by default on Ubuntu).
compat_files_wg: WireGuard® .conf files, from providers, routers and wg-easy
compat_files_ovpn: OpenVPN .ovpn profiles, certificates inside or as separate files
compat_files_no: Not supported: AmneziaWG obfuscation, OpenVPN PKCS#12 bundles
compat_other_text: The macOS app (Apple silicon, macOS 13 and later) is released, the Windows one is being written, both on the same core. Planned: Windows 10 and 11.
